svg.text: What each research question returned
The answer to RQ1 splits at saturation. RQ2 is final. RQ3 splits by resource. RQ4 is cheap in the machine.
RQ1 Latency
Below saturation: medians within 1.6 us.
Paired gap 1.3 us. Too small to bound.
Far tail: Rust lower by 50 us, pooled.
Rust tracks to 448 kops/s, C++ to 392.
At 784 kops/s, C++ finishes 1.7x as much.
Those two picks point at opposite sides.
RQ2 Defects
All 7 in-guarantee classes: compile error.
All 7 boundary classes: compile and fail.
On two of them C++ tools flag what Rust's do not.
Rust drops data races and aliasing errors.
It does not drop race conditions, lock order,
leaks, wrapping, or a failed worker's blast.
RQ3 Resources
Language RSS 1.4 to 2.5 MiB, all hosts.
Allocator 1.5 to 2.4 MiB, either language.
Comparable on bare metal. Guest ratio does not travel.
CPU at 56 kops/s: Rust at most 5.1 pp less.
CPU past saturation: sign flips. Do not mix the two.
RQ4 Adoption
Seam: 11 entries, 9 unsafe functions.
Per-call bound 10.91% of a real signal.
54% of the Rust build is crates.
Size gap is a linkage policy. Order flips if matched.
C++ leads the single-file edit and compile loop.
Taken as a set these support a narrow claim, for stateful, concurrent, partitionable control-plane services of this kind.
